close_reason: Expanded SharingBackend trait-level rustdoc with two new sections: (1) Caller identity (foundation seam) — points at JmapBackend::principal_id supertrait method as the sole authorization input, warns that the default None impl makes RFC 9670 myRights unimplementable, exempts single-user dev/test backends and the reference MemoryBackend, notes the workspace-load-bearing nature of this trait's caller-identity contract since it is the canonical myRights propagation source for mail/calendars/tasks/contacts/filenode. (2) Permission enforcement (backend canonical) — restates the foundation rule that handlers do no permission checking, defense-in-depth pre-checks are optional, backend MUST re-verify atomically. Intra-doc link to principal_id verified resolvable on JmapBackend supertrait. clippy clean, fmt clean, tests green. Doc warnings unchanged (only 2 pre-existing JMAP-23su intra-doc-link warnings in principal.rs, not introduced).
description:
**Location**: `crate-jmap-sharing-server/src/backend.rs:50-61`.

**The gap**: the `SharingBackend` trait-level rustdoc reads:

> Storage backend for JMAP Sharing method handlers (RFC 9670).
>
> Implementors provide the actual data access; the method handler modules
> in this crate translate between JMAP wire protocol and backend calls.
>
> Read-side operations (`get_objects`, `get_state`, `get_changes`,
> `query_objects`, `query_changes`) are defined on the [`JmapBackend`]
> supertrait. Only write operations and type introspection are here.
>
> This trait is not object-safe by design (generic methods). Use
> `Arc<impl SharingBackend>` when sharing across tasks.

It says nothing about caller identity. This is a contract problem
because:

1. **Workspace AGENTS.md is explicit**: "Caller identity (foundation
   seam)" section pins
   `JmapBackend::principal_id(caller: &Self::CallerCtx) -> Option<&jmap_types::Id>`
   as "the ONLY way the JMAP layer asks 'who is the caller'. No
   alternate path exists, no `caller_identity_blob()` escape hatch, no
   generic claims map."

2. **This crate is the canonical source of `myRights`**: the
   crate-level AGENTS.md says "this crate is the canonical source of
   truth for the `myRights` field that other extension-server crates
   (mail, calendars, tasks, contacts, filenode) propagate to their own
   shareable objects. Every ShareNotification / Principal read must be
   authorized against the caller's effective rights on the target
   principal." That contract is between the trait's implementors and
   the rest of the workspace — and is invisible in the trait doc.

3. **Per-method docs do not pick up the slack**: `destroy_object`
   (lines 145-198) does mention the backend-canonical permission
   rule and points at the AGENTS.md anchor, but `create_object`
   (.33) and `update_object` (.32) do not. A downstream implementor
   who reads only the trait-level doc and a single method doc has no
   path to the foundation seam.

4. **`Option<&Id>` is semantically loaded**: AGENTS.md says "A backend
   that returns `None` from `principal_id` is signalling 'this
   deployment does not honor identity-dependent JMAP semantics'.
   Such a backend CANNOT correctly implement chat role-hierarchy,
   calendar ACLs, sharing/myRights, per-user `$seen` on shared
   mailboxes, or metadata `isPrivate` visibility scoping."

   That last clause includes "sharing/myRights" — meaning a backend
   that wires this trait without overriding `principal_id` ships a
   broken `myRights` impl. The trait doc does not warn the implementor.

**Recommended shape**: add a top-level paragraph block to the trait
doc:

```
/// # Caller identity (foundation seam)
///
/// Per the workspace AGENTS.md "Caller identity (foundation seam)"
/// rule, this trait reads caller identity via the
/// [`JmapBackend::principal_id`] method on the supertrait. The
/// returned `Option<&Id>` is the canonical input to per-object
/// permission enforcement.
///
/// **Production deployments MUST override `principal_id`**. The default
/// impl returns `None`, which signals "this deployment does not honor
/// identity-dependent JMAP semantics". Such a backend cannot correctly
/// implement RFC 9670 `myRights` semantics: every Principal /
/// ShareNotification read SHOULD be authorized against the caller's
/// effective rights on the target principal, and `None` removes the
/// authorization input.
///
/// **Single-user dev backends and test fixtures** may leave the
/// default `None` impl in place. The reference [`memory::MemoryBackend`]
/// does this and is correct for its use case.
```

**Severity**: P3. Not a wire-protocol bug; not an immediate footgun.
A real-world consumer wiring multi-user permissions would discover
this concern through workspace AGENTS.md and the absence at the
trait level wouldn't trap them. But the trait doc is the natural
home for the contract — a downstream implementor reading rustdoc
alone is the audience this finding targets.

**Cookie-cutter propagation**: every extension-server trait
(MailBackend, ChatBackend, CalendarsBackend, etc.) faces the same
gap. The canonical mail-server is the propagation anchor.
title: SharingBackend trait-level rustdoc silent on caller identity — workspace foundation seam principal_id is the canonical authorization input but not surfaced here
